verdict.rationale: Publishing a robots.txt is a fair question for any public web portal like ANEF, so the axis applies. The evidence covers only the front door: a ~3 KB JavaScript shell on the ANEF host and a Cloudflare 403 challenge on the parent ministry site. Neither item mentions a robots.txt file or any crawl-permission policy, so there is no evidence the capability is delivered.

support.subject: As an AI-native founder, the service publishes a real robots.txt, so an agent can know what it may read before fetching anything
